result.title: Message-passing graph persistence
result.summary: Message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) are limited in expressive power by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test. Persistent homology (PH) provides topological descriptors that can complement GNN representations, but existing approaches typically compute persistence separately from the representation learning process. In this paper, we introduce Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), a family of topological descriptors that incorporates message passing into graph filtrations. At each filtration step, node embeddings are updated using the current subgraph and associated with persistence events. These embeddings also determine the representatives of connected components during persistence computation. We prove that MGP is invariant under graph isomorphism and that it is strictly more expressive than the PH-based descriptors it extends. We evaluate MGP on an expressivity benchmark and on several graph classification and regression datasets. Experiments show that MGP outperforms other PH-based descriptors on most of these datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Message-Passing Graph Persistence，将消息传递嵌入图过滤过程，用节点嵌入关联持久事件并决定连通分量代表，证明其同构不变且表达力强于所扩展的 PH 描述子，并在图分类与回归任务上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按过滤步骤更新状态、并以嵌入记录结构持续性与代表元的思路，可能为刻画 latent 推理轨迹的结构稳定性与动态状态摘要提供概念借鉴，但迁移价值需核查。
